proposals.name: DiscontinueExperiment
proposals.reason: Both reports discontinue further processing without describing a physical stopping method. Wait does not express discontinuation, and no cooling, quenching, disposal, or workup can be inferred. The differing extension parameters do not establish identical-contract aliases.

effects: Records discontinuation of further experimental processing.
Asserts no physical change to the mixture.
guards: Preserve the reported scope of discontinuation.
Leave the physical termination method unknown unless explicitly reported.

proposals.name: Add
proposals.reason: The material-introduction effect is already Add; alternate quantity descriptions do not create another physical operation. Preserve independently reported mass, volume, molar amount, loading, equivalents, aliases, and formulation as source annotations without deriving missing quantities or creating duplicate doses. The pre-ligation quotation supports only the introduction component here, not representation of the whole pre-ligation process. Missing required vessel or amount bindings remain unresolved.

proposals.name: Atmosphere
proposals.reason: Explicit argon bubbling establishes atmosphere by a reported method and fits Atmosphere, unlike an environment-only statement. Retain bubbling as the establishment method and 20 minutes as 1200 seconds; do not infer evacuation cycles.

proposals.name: Evaporate
proposals.reason: Removing THF under reduced pressure has the existing volatile-inventory removal effect. Retain the qualitative reduced-pressure condition, but leave numerical pressure, temperature, duration, and vessel binding unknown where unreported.

proposals.name: DistributeLiquidToPlateWells
proposals.reason: Add represents an individual quantified introduction but does not encode the reported per-well distribution over unspecified destination wells. A lossless macro cannot be admitted without well assignments, complete mapping, and executable roundtrip witnesses. The 384-well plate capacity does not establish 384 additions.

effects: Introduces liquid into plate wells according to the reported distribution basis.
guards: Do not infer occupied wells or number of additions from plate capacity.
Keep per-well volume distinct from total or per-solution volume.
Do not infer a liquid-handler identity.

proposals.name: Filter
proposals.reason: Passing material through the reported pad is existing solid–liquid filtration. Preserve the reported medium; the quotation does not identify the retained product stream, so the required keep binding remains unresolved rather than defaulting to filtrate.

proposals.name: AdsorbOnSupport
proposals.reason: Loading reaction material onto silica has an adsorption endpoint not supplied by Add or opaque terminal Purify. No particular mixing, transfer, or evaporation sequence is reported, so a known-operation macro would invent a preparation method. Subsequent chromatography remains separate.

effects: Loads the specified material onto the adsorbent support.
guards: Do not infer support mass or an adsorption technique.
Do not include subsequent purification in this action.

proposals.name: RecordAnalyticalObservation
proposals.reason: The report records a GC-MS composition finding rather than prescribing synthesis or a sampling procedure. No registered operation records analytical results; keep this information-recording effect distinct from performing an analytical examination.

effects: Records reported analytical composition without changing material inventory.
guards: Do not infer isolation, sampling, or analytical operating conditions.

proposals.name: SetHeatingBlockTemperature
proposals.reason: The quotation identifies a preheated block at 80 °C, not a measured sample temperature. HeatChill on the reaction vessel would conflate hardware setpoint with sample temperature. Retain this as a heater-state candidate, without inferring the preheating duration or a sample-temperature endpoint.

effects: Specifies the heating block temperature setting independently of sample temperature.
guards: Do not equate block setpoint with sample temperature.
Do not infer stirring, preheating duration, or a temperature-control procedure.

proposals.name: AnalyzeReactionMaterial
proposals.reason: These phrases describe analytical examination or assessment and reported findings, not material-processing operations. None of the registered operations supplies this effect. A shared candidate can preserve LCMS versus GC/MS versus an unspecified method and retain completion, conversion, decomposition, and isolation findings without turning those findings into physical actions.

effects: Obtains analytical information about reaction material.
Records reported findings without asserting synthesis or isolation.
guards: Preserve analytical method identity; an unspecified method remains unknown.
Do not infer sampling, transfer, sample quantity, or analytical conditions.
Treat completion, decomposition, and isolation outcomes as reported observations, not processing instructions.
Do not convert absence of detected product into an unreported quantitative yield.

proposals.name: AnalyzeCrudeByNmrWithInternalStandard
proposals.reason: All three reports describe crude proton NMR with an internal standard and reported selectivity and analytical yield. This analytical mode is absent from the registry and remains distinct from generic reaction monitoring. The extension contracts differ in required fields, so they are not identical-contract aliases; notably, no internal-standard amount is supplied by these quotations.

effects: Obtains an NMR analytical observation of the crude sample using an internal standard.
Records reported ratios and analytical yield without implying isolation.
guards: Preserve ratio order and component assignments.
Do not infer internal-standard quantity or its addition procedure.
Keep analytical yield distinct from isolated yield.

proposals.name: Irradiate
proposals.reason: The mention denotes the existing optical-exposure action. It supplies no duration, wavelength, power, color, or vessel binding, so reuse identifies semantics only and does not establish a complete operation instance.

proposals.name: Purify
proposals.reason: Both quotations describe chromatographic purification already represented by Purify. Stationary phase and eluent composition describe the associated method, not a second media-application action. Retain the distinct 15% and 12% compositions as method annotations; do not infer percentage basis, packing, or solvent preparation.

proposals.name: Atmosphere
proposals.reason: These purported device observations identify gas environments, not apparatus. Reuse Atmosphere in its context-only environment mode, preserving nitrogen for the first two observations and argon for the third. Neither gas-control hardware nor a purge or evacuation method is established.

proposals.name: Stir
proposals.reason: Two minutes of stirring is the existing Stir effect with duration 120 seconds. Preserve room temperature as qualitative context without inventing a numerical temperature or stirring rate; vessel binding still requires context.

proposals.name: Transfer
proposals.reason: The reported movement into a capped microwave vial fits Transfer, with syringe delivery retained as context. The quotation alone does not supply source vessel or amount, so those bindings remain unresolved; the destination does not imply microwave irradiation.

proposals.name: Wait
proposals.reason: Wait can retain the reported 15-minute elapsed interval as 900 seconds without implying stirring or heating. It represents only the timing component and does not by itself represent the stated pre-ligation chemistry.

proposals.name: GasChromatographyMassSpectrometryInstrument
proposals.reason: All three observations explicitly name GC/MS, a common analytical apparatus type absent from the existing families. Keep this family distinct from LC-MS and HPLC. No manufacturer, model, configuration, or interchangeability is established.

proposals.name: LiquidChromatographyMassSpectrometryInstrument
proposals.reason: LCMS and LC/MS identify the same common coupled analytical apparatus type, absent from the existing families. They do not establish a column, operating conditions, instrument identity, or interchangeability; GC/MS remains a separate family.

proposals.name: HplcInstrument
proposals.reason: Both quotations explicitly identify HPLC despite generic device labels. No existing apparatus family covers this analytical type. HPLC alone does not establish mass-spectrometric detection, instrument configuration, or interchangeability with another family member.
